# Git LFS

<!-- Generated by tools/clientrecipes from src/gitlfs.json; edit the source. -->

Read the [common setup and credential rules](README.md) first. [All recipes](index.md).

Client: **Git LFS 3.8.1**. Registered classes: **local, remote, virtual, federated**.

Endpoint: `${AW_URL}/artifactory/api/lfs/${AW_REPO}`

## Before connecting

- An existing producer Git repository and a separately hosted Git origin.
- Commit .lfsconfig and .gitattributes so a consumer discovers the LFS endpoint.
- AW_GIT_ORIGIN is your separate Git-host clone URL. Supply that host's own credentials through its normal scoped mechanism; never use the artifactweave token for it.

Authentication: Use an access or reference token as the HTTP Basic password, with AW_USER equal to its subject. The subject needs read permission for installation and deploy permission for publication on the selected repository; token scopes cannot exceed that identity. The same clients also accept a user password when Basic password authentication is enabled. Use HTTPS.

Fresh client state: Create a new AW_WORK with mktemp -d for every run; client configuration, downloads and caches in the commands stay under this directory. Do not reuse it to prove a fresh download. Remove the temporary directory after use.

## Configure

Run in the producer Git repository, with AW_WORK and runtime variables kept for the consumer. .lfsconfig contains only the endpoint and may be committed; the helper resolves credentials from environment.

```sh
umask 077
AW_WORK=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$AW_WORK/home"
export LFS_USER="$AW_USER" LFS_PASSWORD="$AW_TOKEN"
export LFS_URL="$AW_URL/artifactory/api/lfs/$AW_REPO"
git lfs install --local
git config credential.useHttpPath true
git config "credential.$LFS_URL.helper" '!f() { echo "username=$LFS_USER"; echo "password=$LFS_PASSWORD"; }; f'
printf '[lfs]\n\turl = %s\n' "$LFS_URL" > .lfsconfig
```

## Publish

Classes: **local, federated**. Publish to a local or one-node federated repository. Remote repositories are read-through caches; select the local deployment member when reading through a virtual.

Configure origin to your separate Git host first. The LFS push stores object bytes in artifactweave; the Git push publishes the committed pointers, .gitattributes and .lfsconfig for fresh clones. Git-host credentials are separate.

```sh
git lfs track "*.bin"
git add .gitattributes .lfsconfig asset.bin
git commit -m "Publish LFS asset"
git lfs push origin HEAD
git push origin HEAD
```

## Install or resolve

Classes: **local, remote, virtual, federated**. Select a local, remote, virtual or one-node federated repository with read permission. Dependencies must also be available through that repository.

AW_GIT_ORIGIN is the Git host URL; its authentication is separate. The fresh clone has an empty .git/lfs/objects cache.

```sh
env HOME="$AW_WORK/home" GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 git clone "$AW_GIT_ORIGIN" "$AW_WORK/consumer"
env HOME="$AW_WORK/home" git -C "$AW_WORK/consumer" config credential.useHttpPath true
env HOME="$AW_WORK/home" git -C "$AW_WORK/consumer" config "credential.$LFS_URL.helper" '!f() { echo "username=$LFS_USER"; echo "password=$LFS_PASSWORD"; }; f'
env HOME="$AW_WORK/home" git -C "$AW_WORK/consumer" lfs install --local
env HOME="$AW_WORK/home" git -C "$AW_WORK/consumer" lfs pull
```

## Limits

Classes outside **local, remote, virtual, federated** are not registered for this format. Commands above apply only to each operation's listed classes. Federated evidence is for one node; it does not establish cross-vendor replication.

- LFS is object transfer and locking; it is not a Git smart-HTTP or SSH server.
- Do not use the LFS API URL as the Git clone URL.
- Use a fresh clone to prove remote transfer; a previously hydrated working tree is not proof.
- The artifactweave helper is scoped to the LFS endpoint including its path. Do not configure an unscoped helper that returns the token for arbitrary Git hosts.
